title: Tiered egress weighted shift checklist (gradual regional traffic egress)
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic checklist and quick-reference for executing a gradual, weighted egress shift away from a degraded region to warm-standby capacity in another region. The intent is low-risk progressive migration (small increments, validate, repeat) versus a blunt cutover. Keep this doc lightweight — embed links to more detailed playbooks when needed.

Context / when to use:
- Regional degradation where primary region latency or error rate exceeds alert thresholds but control plane remains responsive (examples: elevated queueing on EU cluster, partial AZ CPU pressure).
- You have a healthy warm-standby (pre-warmed model instances, warm KV cache, global edge routing available) in target region.
- Desired outcome: move production traffic gradually with tight validation gates (every step is reversible).

Pre-flight (15–30m) — mandatory before any traffic weight changes:
- Confirm warm-standby health: target region model processes at target concurrency, token throughput stable. Commands: infra-health check (link to infra runbook).
- KV cache warm-up: run synthetic requests that exercise typical prompt prefixes to prime KV caches. Script: tools/prime_kv.sh --profile prod --region target.
- Verify autoscaling headroom: ensure dedicated pool or autoscaler can handle +X% traffic without queueing. Check dashboard: Console -> Dedicated -> Pools -> target-pool -> Current headroom.
- Adjust DNS TTLs and LB session settings: set Route53/edge TTL to 30s (if currently >60s). Documented command samples below.
- Notify stakeholders: post to #sre-ops and to customer-facing status if risk of visible errors (template included in linked artifacts).
- Pre-set monitoring queries and a “canary dashboard” showing 1) p50/p95 latency, 2) 5xx rate, 3) CPU/GPU utilization, 4) queue depth, 5) KV cache hit rate, 6) errors by model and route.

Shift plan (recommended default):
- Increment size: 5% -> 10% -> 20% -> 40% -> 60% -> 80% -> 100%. Smaller increments if service is high-risk.
- Dwell time per increment: minimum 3 minutes + verification window (suggest 10 minutes for high-risk routes).
- Total expected time: ~30–60 minutes depending on dwell windows.

Traffic-weight change procedure (Route53/Traffic Manager example):
1) Set DNS/traffic manager TTL to 30s in advance.
2) Apply first weight change: update weighted routing policy (increase target region weight by 5%, decrease source by same amount). Example AWS change-batch (replace placeholders):
   aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-primary","Weight":95,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"1.2.3.4"}]}} , {"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-standby","Weight":5,"TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"5.6.7.8"}]}}]}'
3) Wait for propagation (2x TTL) then begin validation window.
4) Run synthetic validation and compare metrics on the canary dashboard.

Validation gates (must pass to continue):
- 5xx rate on target region routes < 0.5x baseline spike threshold AND not increasing over dwell window.
- p95 latency delta relative to baseline < configured cap (suggest 2x baseline p95 or absolute cap e.g., 400ms).
- CPU/GPU utilization steady (no sustained >85% on target instances).
- KV cache miss-rate acceptable (no >30% increase sustained).
- No customer-facing error reports or significant uptick in CS tickets.

Rollback policy (on failed gate):
- Immediately revert weights to previous stable percentages. Use the same change-batch but swap values.
- If DNS propagation delay causes lag in effect, place traffic filter at edge (NGINX/Envoy route-level deny) to quickly re-route if available.
- If degradation persists despite rollback, escalate to SRE on-call lead and open incident channel.

Edge cases and operational notes:
- Sticky sessions / cookies: some clients have long-lived connections — verify the proportion of sessions that are sticky. If large, consider draining connections at app or LB level (graceful connection draining) rather than DNS-only.
- Client IP-based routing: check fingerprinting logic; ensure target region has correct geo/whitelist rules.
- Model variant compatibility: if fallback uses a quantized variant, include quality checks (automated prompts) as part of the validation window.
- Rate-limiting and quotas: ensure global quota counters are synced or isolated per-region to avoid global throttling.

Quick commands & snippets (reference):
- Prime KV cache: scripts/prime_kv.sh --region us-west-2 --model redwood-v2 --concurrency 20 --duration 120s
- Verify processes: kubectl --context prod-us-west get pods -l app=model-server | grep Running
- Change Route53 weights: see example above (keep a local copy of previous weights).
- Set TTL via CLI: aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://set-ttl-30.json

Post-shift stabilization (30–120m):
- Continue monitoring the canary dashboard for at least 1 hour after finalizing 100% cutover.
- Run a sampling of customer-critical prompts through the target region to validate output quality.
- Update runbook to mark warm-standby as the new primary if desired, or start rollback-to-normal sequence when source region is healthy.

Decision log (example entries):
- 2025-02-14 11:05 UTC — observed EU queue depth rising; auto-scaler reacted but latency p95 degraded to 650ms.
- 2025-02-14 11:25 UTC — warm-standby in us-west healthy; decided to attempt 5% shift with 10m dwell. Owner: Asha.

Open questions / follow-ups (action items):
- (ACTIONS) Add automated KV warm-wake on rate-limited background job to reduce manual priming steps. Owner: Miguel. Due: 2025-03-10.
- Investigate sticky session footprint and whether to adopt per-request statelessness for quicker cutovers. Owner: Lena. Due: 2025-03-01.
- Create a templated DNS weight change tool that records old weights and provides one-click revert. Owner: Infra Eng. Due: 2025-04-01.

Notes to self / troubleshooting tips:
- If target region shows high GPU wait time despite low app CPU, check model artifact mismatch (occasionally a different build slips into warm-standby).
- When in doubt, slow down: smaller increments and longer dwell times almost always reduce blast radius.
- Keep an offline copy of the last-known-good Route53 change-batch in case API calls are rate-limited during incident.

Attachments & templates (in linked_artifacts):
- DNS weight change CLI template (change-batch examples).
- Incident Slack template for customer-facing status updates.
- Canary dashboard link and queries.

If anything in this checklist is unclear during an active shift, pause and call the SRE lead. Better to hold traffic steady for 10–15 minutes than to oscillate weights and create cascading autoscaling churn.

End of checklist.

-- Asha (SRE)
